## Overview: Why Reading Raw Data Matters in Business Analytics

In **BAN 3083**, data rarely arrives in a clean SQL table. Often, corporate ERP systems (like SAP, Oracle, or SAS exports) dump raw text files with:

- **Banner headers** at the top of the file ("Report Generated on...")
- **Spaces and symbols in column names** (`Gross Revenue ($)`, `Store ID #`)
- **Numbers stored as text** because of dollar signs (`$142,500.50`) or percent signs (`2.1%`)
- **Inconsistent missing value codes** (`N/A`, `MISSING`, `-999`)

In this module, we will read these raw files into R, clean them on import, audit their quality, and then display the results with **tables (`skimr`, `gt`)** and **charts (`ggplot2`)**.

---

## Part 1: What Happens When You Import a Messy CSV Naively?

Always look at the raw text *before* importing it.

```{r inspect-raw-lines}
# Read the first 6 raw lines of text to inspect the file before importing
read_lines("data/messy_erp_sales.csv", n_max = 6)
```

Notice two major problems:

1. **Lines 1 and 2** are report banners, not column headers.
2. Missing values are coded as `"N/A"`, `"MISSING"`, and `"-999"`, and revenue has `"$"` and commas.

If we run a naive `read_csv()`, the table is ruined. This chunk turns warnings **on** so you can see the parsing problems R reports (in your own work, never ignore these):

```{r naive-import, warning=TRUE, message=TRUE}
naive_df <- read_csv("data/messy_erp_sales.csv")
naive_df

# problems() lists every row R could not parse the way it expected
problems(naive_df)
```

---

## Part 2: Reading & Cleaning Raw Data the Right Way (`read_csv` + `janitor`)

We fix the structural problems right inside `read_csv()` using three arguments:

- `skip = 2`: skips the 2 banner lines (like `FIRSTOBS=3` in SAS).
- `na = missing_codes`: converts every custom missing code (`""`, `NA`, `N/A`, `MISSING`, `-999`) into a true R `NA`.
- `col_types`: tells R exactly what each column is, so it never guesses. We read the currency and percent columns as text (because of the `$`, `,` and `%`) and `Total Transactions` as an integer.

Then we pipe (`|>`) into:

- `janitor::clean_names()`: turns `"Gross Revenue ($)"` into snake_case `gross_revenue`, `"Store ID #"` into `store_id_number`, and `"Return Rate (%)"` into `return_rate_percent`.
- `readr::parse_number()`: strips `"$"`, `","`, and `"%"` so revenue and return rates become real numbers.

```{r clean-import}
clean_sales <- read_csv(
  file = "data/messy_erp_sales.csv",
  skip = 2,
  na = missing_codes,
  col_types = cols(
    .default = col_character(),
    `Total Transactions` = col_integer()
  )
) |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    gross_revenue   = parse_number(gross_revenue),
    return_rate_pct = parse_number(return_rate_percent)
  ) |>
  select(-return_rate_percent) |>
  rename(store_id = store_id_number)

clean_sales
```

---

## Part 3: Displaying Data Quality with Diagnostic Tables (`skimr` & `janitor`)

Before running any analysis, display a **Data Quality Audit Table** to verify data types and missing values (`n_missing`). You should see exactly one missing value each in `gross_revenue` (STR-104), `total_transactions` (STR-105) and `return_rate_pct` (STR-107).

```{r skim-audit-table}
skim(clean_sales)
```

A two-way **frequency table** of `store_region` vs. `audit_status` using `janitor::tabyl()`:

```{r tabyl-status}
clean_sales |>
  tabyl(store_region, audit_status) |>
  adorn_totals(c("row", "col")) |>
  adorn_percentages("row") |>
  adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 1) |>
  adorn_ns()
```

---

## Part 4: Reading Custom Delimited Files (`read_delim`)

When logistics or mainframe systems export data separated by pipes (`|`) or tabs (`\t`) instead of commas (like `DLM='|'` in SAS `INFILE`), use `read_delim()`:

```{r read-pipe}
shipments <- read_delim(
  file = "data/vendor_shipments_pipe.txt",
  delim = "|",
  col_types = cols(
    Shipment_ID = col_character(),
    Warehouse_Hub = col_character(),
    Carrier = col_character(),
    Boxes_Shipped = col_integer(),
    Freight_Cost_USD = col_double(),
    Delivery_Days = col_integer()
  )
) |>
  clean_names()

shipments
```

---

## Part 5: Displaying Imported Data with Executive Tables (`gt`) & Plots (`ggplot2`)

Keep the data numeric in R and apply formatting only at the display layer (`gt` for tables, `scales` for charts).

### 1. Executive Summary Table (`gt`)

```{r gt-regional-summary}
clean_sales |>
  group_by(store_region) |>
  summarize(
    stores = n(),
    avg_revenue = mean(gross_revenue, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_transactions = sum(total_transactions, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_return_rate = mean(return_rate_pct, na.rm = TRUE) / 100
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(avg_revenue)) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Regional Store Performance Summary",
    subtitle = "Cleaned ERP Export (BAN 3083 Data Audit)"
  ) |>
  fmt_currency(columns = avg_revenue, currency = "USD") |>
  fmt_number(columns = total_transactions, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = avg_return_rate, decimals = 1) |>
  cols_label(
    store_region = "Region",
    stores = "# Stores",
    avg_revenue = "Mean Gross Revenue",
    total_transactions = "Total Transactions",
    avg_return_rate = "Mean Return Rate"
  )
```

### 2. Visualizing Store Revenue & Audit Status (`ggplot2`)

```{r plot-cleaned-sales}
clean_sales |>
  drop_na(gross_revenue) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(store_id, gross_revenue), y = gross_revenue, fill = store_region)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar()) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Gross Revenue by Store After Parsing Currency Strings",
    subtitle = "Store STR-104 is missing: its revenue was coded 'N/A' and became NA on import",
    x = "Store ID",
    y = "Gross Revenue (USD)",
    fill = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

## Part 6: Your Turn! (Practice Exercises)

### Exercise 1: Summarize & Format the Pipe-Delimited Logistics Data

Using the `shipments` data from Part 4, run the chunk below to build a `gt` table of total boxes shipped and average freight cost by `carrier`. Then add a column of your own (for example, average delivery days).

```{r ex1-carrier-table}
shipments |>
  group_by(carrier) |>
  summarize(
    num_shipments = n(),
    total_boxes = sum(boxes_shipped),
    avg_freight_cost = mean(freight_cost_usd)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Logistics Carrier Summary") |>
  fmt_currency(columns = avg_freight_cost, currency = "USD")
```

### Exercise 2: Plot Freight Cost vs. Boxes Shipped

Run and customize the scatterplot below:

```{r ex2-shipment-plot}
ggplot(shipments, aes(x = boxes_shipped, y = freight_cost_usd, color = carrier, size = delivery_days)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar()) +
  labs(
    title = "Freight Cost vs. Shipment Volume by Carrier",
    x = "Boxes Shipped",
    y = "Freight Cost (USD)",
    color = "Carrier",
    size = "Delivery Days"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Exercise 3: Import the Branch Audit File (Lecture 2 Slide 5)

`branch_audit.csv` has the same problems as the ERP file: 2 banner lines, symbols in the headers, `$` and `%` text, and `N/A` / `-999` missing codes. The import is done for you below. Run it, check that `skim()` reports one missing value each in `gross_rev` and `defect_percent`, then write your own `gt` table or `ggplot2` chart in the empty chunk.

```{r ex3-branch-import}
branch_audit <- read_csv(
  file = "data/branch_audit.csv",
  skip = 2,
  na = missing_codes,
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
) |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    gross_rev = parse_number(gross_rev),
    defect_percent = parse_number(defect_percent)
  )

branch_audit
skim(branch_audit)
```

```{r ex3-your-turn}
# Your turn: summarize or plot branch_audit (e.g., gross_rev by region)

```

## How to Publish to RPubs & Submit Your URL on Canvas

1. **Add Your Name**: On line 3 of this file (`author:`), replace `[Type Your Name Here]` with your name and save (`Ctrl+S` / `Cmd+S`).
2. **Click the green `▶` button on the chunk below.** It knits your report to HTML, uploads it to **RPubs.com**, and prints a `http://rpubs.com/publish/claim/...` link under the chunk.
3. **Click that link.** RPubs opens in a new tab (sign in or create a free account the first time, then click **Continue**). Copy your final `https://rpubs.com/your_username/...` URL from the address bar and paste it into **Canvas**.

```{r publish-to-rpubs, eval=FALSE}
# CLICK THE GREEN PLAY BUTTON ON THE RIGHT OF THIS CHUNK TO PUBLISH

# Make sure the publishing package is installed
if (!requireNamespace("rsconnect", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("rsconnect")

# Step 1: Knit your latest work into an HTML report
rmarkdown::render("Week02_Reading_Raw_Data.Rmd", quiet = TRUE)

# Step 2: Upload the HTML report to RPubs.com
upload_result <- rsconnect::rpubsUpload(
  title = "BAN 3083: Week 2 Reading Raw Data",
  contentFile = "Week02_Reading_Raw_Data.html",
  originalDoc = "Week02_Reading_Raw_Data.Rmd"
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("SUCCESS! CLICK THE LINK BELOW TO CLAIM YOUR RPUBS PAGE:\n")
cat(upload_result$continueUrl, "\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
```
